content:
Ever imagined generating stunning concept art with just a few clicks? What if you could customize it by choosing your favorite objects, materials, and artistic styles—no Photoshop, no drawing skills required?

This tutorial walks you through building an AI-powered concept art generator using Streamlit and the OpenAI Image API, letting users generate and download custom artwork from a web interface.

🧠 What Are We Building?

A Streamlit web app that allows users to:

  • Select an object (e.g., Robot, Dragon, Car)
  • Choose a material (e.g., Metal, Crystal, Rusty Metal)
  • Pick an art style (e.g., Cartoonish, Fantasy, Retro-futurism)
  • Generate AI-powered concept art instantly
  • Download the image as a PNG

🛠️ Tools and Libraries Used

  • Streamlit – to create the web interface
  • OpenAI – for generating the concept art
  • Pillow (PIL) – for image processing
  • Requests & Certifi – for secure HTTP requests

📦 Prerequisites

Make sure you have the following installed:

pip install streamlit openai pillow requests certifi

Also, store your OpenAI API key securely in a file named apikey.py:

apikey = "your_openai_api_key_here"

🧩 Code Breakdown

Here’s what the core parts of the code are doing:

1. Environment & API Setup

os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

We authenticate the OpenAI client using your API key.

2. User Interface with Streamlit

st.title("AI-Generated Concept Art with Object and Material Customization")

We build an interactive UI with dropdowns for:

  • Object types
  • Materials
  • Artistic styles
  • Image sizes

3. Prompt Engineering

full_prompt = f"A {object_type.lower()} made of {material.lower()} in a {style.lower()} style"

This dynamic prompt tells the AI exactly what kind of image to generate. For example:

“A dragon made of crystal in a fantasy style”

4. Image Generation and Display

response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)

OpenAI’s API generates an image based on your custom prompt and returns a URL. We then fetch the image and display it with:

st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

5. Download Functionality

st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name="your_file.png", mime="image/png")

This allows users to save their creation with one click.

🎬 Demo Preview

Once you run the app with:

streamlit run your_script.py

You’ll be able to:

  1. Select "Spaceship", "Shiny chrome", and "Futuristic" style.
  2. Click "Generate Image".
  3. View and download your AI-generated artwork!

🔮 Creative Possibilities

This tool is ideal for:

  • Game developers prototyping asset ideas
  • Writers looking for visual inspiration
  • Artists & designers experimenting with new aesthetics
  • Educators teaching prompt engineering and creative AI

🚀 Final Thoughts

AI tools are rapidly transforming creative workflows. By combining OpenAI's powerful image generation with Streamlit's ease of use, you’ve just built a tool that can turn imagination into art—no sketching required.

"Creativity is not a skill, it's a prompt away."

💡 Want More?

You could enhance this app by:

  • Adding background scene generation
  • Creating random prompts with a surprise button
  • Using user-uploaded sketches as inspiration

Python Code:

import os

import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# Define object types, materials, and artistic styles
objects = ["Robot", "Spaceship", "Sword", "House", "Car", "Tree", "Dragon", "Castle"]
materials = ["Metal", "Wood", "Stone", "Crystal", "Glass", "Plastic", "Shiny chrome", "Rusty metal"]
styles = ["Photorealistic", "Sketch", "Cartoonish", "Futuristic", "Fantasy", "Post-apocalyptic", "Retro-futurism"]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("AI-Generated Concept Art with Object and Material Customization")
st.write("Create concept art by specifying objects, materials, and artistic styles for your image.")

# User input: Object, Material, Artistic Style, and Image Size
object_type = st.selectbox("Select an object to generate:", objects)
material = st.selectbox("Select a material for the object:", materials)
style = st.selectbox("Select an artistic style:", styles)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Image"):
    # Combine the inputs into a full prompt
    full_prompt = f"A {object_type.lower()} made of {material.lower()} in a {style.lower()} style"
    st.write(f"Generating image for: '{full_prompt}'")

    # Generate the image
    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

    # Fetch and display the image
    img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
    img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))

    st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

    # Provide an option to download the image
    img_bytes = BytesIO()
    img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
    img_bytes.seek(0)
    st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{object_type.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_{material.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_{style.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.png", mime="image/png")
